IS : 3291 - 1968

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR THREAD TAKE UP CAMS FOR SEWING MACHINES FOR HOUSEHOLD PURPOSES

(First Revision)
0. F O R E W O R D
0.1 This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 29 August 1968, after the draft finalized by the Sewing Machines Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 0.2 This standard was first issued in 1965. The present revision has been taken up to incorporate one more type of thread take up cam which is being manufactured by a section of the manufacturers in the country. 0.3 This standard covers the requirements for thread take up cams for sewing machines, and is intended to assist in regulating the quality of indigenous thread take up cams. This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on sewing machines and their components, being prepared on the recommendation of the Tariff Commission and at the instance of Development Commissioner for Small Scale Industries ( Ministry of Industrial Development & Company Affairs ), Government of India. 0.4 Non-metric threads have also been specified as an interim measure till the complete changeover to metric system takes place. The manufacturers have agreed to adopt ISO metric screw threads at an early date. 0.5 While preparing this standard, assistance has been derived from JISB 9036-1960 'Thread take up cam of sewing machine for home use' issued by Japanese Industrial Standards Committee. 0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised).

3

IS : 3291 - 1968 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard specifies the requirements for two types of thread take up cams for sewing machines for household purposes. 1.1.1 This standard does not cover the thread take up cams used in industrial and special purpose sewing machines. 2. NOMENCLATURE 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the nomenclature as given in Fig. 1 shall apply.

FIG.

1

NOMENCLATURE OF THREAD TAKE UP CAMS FOR SEWING MACHINES

3. MATERIAL 3.1 The thread take up cams shall be made from any suitable material, such as grey cast iron conforming to Grade 20 of IS : 210-1962* or steel, such as 13S25 of Schedule III of IS : 1570-1961. 4. DIMENSIONS 4.1 The main dimensions for thread take up cams shall be as given in Tables 1 and 2. The recommended paraxial dimensions for the scroll profile with respect to the front face of thread take up cams are given in Appendix A.
*Specification for grey iron castings ( revised ). Schedules for wrought steels for general engineering purposes.

IS : 3291 - 1968 5. TOLERANCES 5.1 The error in squareness of the axis of arm shaft hole with respect to the front face of the cam shall not exceed 0.15 mm per 100 mm. 5.2 The error in the squareness of the axis of arm shaft hole with respect to the scroll profile shall be within 0.15 mm per 100 mm. 5.3 Tolerances on untoleranced dimensions shall conform to fine grade tolerance of IS : 2102-1962*. 6. WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 6.1 The scroll and the arm shaft hole of the thread take up cam shall be machined to a fine finish without any line mark. 6.2 The thread take up cam shall be well finished without any crack, flaw blow hole, rust or other defects. 6.3 The front face of the thread take up cam shall be so finished as to be perpendicular to the axis of the cam. 7. MARKING 7.1 The thread take up cams shall be marked with the manufacturer's name or trade-mark. 7.1.1 The thread take up cam may also be marked with the Standard Mark. NOTE -- The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 8. PACKING 8.1 Each thread take up cam shall be given a suitable antirust coating or wrapped in vapour phase inhibitor paper (commonly known as VPI paper). The wrapped thread take up cams shall be securely packed in cardboard cartons in accordance with the best prevalent trade practice. Each carton shall bear the manufacturers' name or trade-mark, the type, the size and the description of contents. *Recommendations for machining deviations for dimensions without specified tolerances.(Since revised).

7

IS : 3291 - 1968 8.1.1 The cartons may also be marked with the ISI Certification Mark (see Note under 7.1.1 ). 9. SAMPLING 9.1 Unless otherwise agreed upon between the supplier and the purchaser, the sampling plan as given in Appendix B shall be followed. For further information reference may be made to I S : 2500 ( Part I )-1963*.

APPENDIX (Clause 9.1)
B-1. SCALE OF SAMPLING

B

SCALE OF SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY

B-1.1 Lot -- In any consignment, all the thread take up cams of the same type manufactured from the same material under essentially similar conditions of manufacture, shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. B-1.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements of the specification, tests shall be carried out for each lot separately. The number of thread take up cams to be selected at random for this purpose shall be in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 5.
TABLE 5 SCALE OF SAMPLING AND PERMISSIBLE NUMBER OF DEFECTIVES FOR DIMENSIONS, TOLERANCES WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH Sample Size Permissible No. of Defectives* (3) 0

NUMBER OF THREAD

CAMS IN

TAKE UP THE LOT

N Up 16 41 111 301 501 801 1 301 (1) to 15 ,, 40 ,, 110 ,, 300 ,, 500 ,, 800 ,, :1300 and above

n

(2) 5

8 13 20 32 50 80 125

0 0 1 1 2 3 5

*This ensures that lots containing only one and a half percent or less defectives will be accepted most of the times.

B-1.3 The thread take up cams shall be selected at random, in order to ensure the randomness of selection, the following procedure is recommended for use: Starting from any thread take up cam in a lot, count them in one order as 1, 2, 3, up to r and so on, where r is the integral part of N/n ( N being the number of thread take up cams in the lot 11

IS : 3291 - 1968 and n being the number of thread take up cams in the sample ). Every rth thread take up cam thus counted shall be selected to constitute a sample. B-2. CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY B-2.1 The thread take up cams selected according to B-1.2 and B-1.3 shall be examined for dimensions ( see 4 ), tolerances ( see 5 ) and workmanship and finish ( see 6 ). If the number of thread take up cams failing to meet one or more of the requirements mentioned above is less than or equal to the permissible number of defectives given in col 3 of Table 5 the lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of these characteristics, otherwise not.
